newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan premium widens ahead of fiscal year-end.
newsitem.headline: Japan premium widens ahead of fiscal year-end.

text.p: The Japan premium -- the extra cost Japanese banks pay for raising funds in the eurodollar interbank market -- widened this week due to fiscal year-end fund raising pressure, bank traders said on Thursday.

Japanese banks are paying around 5.9 percent for one-month eurodollar deposits, which is about 0.25 percentage point above the prevailing rate. This compares with a premium of about 0.19 percentage point last Friday.
However, the premium is likely to shrink in the coming days as the seasonal fund-raising pressure has already peaked, traders said.

"The one-month eurodollar rate is higher due to a seasonal factor, but this factor will be gone from Friday as the value date (settlement date) will move to April starting tomorrow," said a trader at a major city bank.

Traders said the premium on three-month eurodollar deposits had already fallen back to around 0.16 percentage point on Thursday. It stood at around 0.22 percentage point on Wednesday, compared with around 0.125 percentage point last Friday.
"Major Japanese banks were well aware that the rates will rise at the fiscal year-end, so they did their fund-raising in advance," said the trader.
